description: `not` wrapping a `properties` keyword with two properties, the second a dangling `$ref`: Python's own `next(iter_errors(instance), None) is None` (`not`'s own lazy `is_valid` building block) pulls exactly one value from the whole nested generator tree, so the first property's own `type` violation is the only one it ever sees -- the second property's dangling `$ref` is never reached, never raises, and `not` itself reports `schema_invalid` from the first property's own mismatch alone, cleanly.
